"timeout-minutes" is not set at this job. Set it to avoid wasting runner minutes when the job hangs
jdx/mise-action restores a cache although the job runs "gh release create", so a poisoned cache entry can end up in the published artifacts. set "cache: false", or set "cache-mode: none" on the job

"actions: write" is granted to every job of the workflow, which lets any of them cancel and re-run workflow runs and manage caches and artifacts. set "permissions: {}" at the workflow level and grant "actions: write" only to the job which needs it

trigger "issue_comment" is dangerous: it runs in the context of the default branch with a write token and secrets and can be started by anyone who can comment. check the permission of the commenter and never run code of the pull request

actions/checkout is given secret "SITE_DEPLOY_KEY" as "ssh-key". this credential does not expire and can reach more than this job needs, and unless "persist-credentials: false" is set it is also left in the git config of the workspace for every later step to read. use the default GITHUB_TOKEN for this repository. to reach other repositories or to push something that starts other workflows, use a short-lived token from a GitHub App (actions/create-github-app-token) or a fine-grained personal access token limited to the repositories it needs, and keep it in a secret of a protected environment

trigger "workflow_run" is dangerous: it runs in the context of the default branch with a write token and secrets, but processes artifacts and metadata produced by a run that a fork may control. consider a reusable workflow called with "workflow_call" instead, and never trust the artifacts or the event payload
